entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Marcus Fulvius Bambalio was a nobleman of the Fulvia gens of ancient Rome, who lived in the 1st century BCE. Based on his cognomen, and invective directed at him by his contemporaries, he must have had a speech disorder. It is unclear what exactly his social rank was; scholars disagree on whether he was or was not a nobilis, as contemporary writers would draw unfavorable comparisons between Fulvius's social rank and that of his son-in-law, Mark Antony.
